svg.text: C1-C MOTORISED DRAWER UNITS around a shared shaft (rejected)
Unmodified drawer fridges and freezers face a shaft; a lift pulls a drawer out and the gallery hoist picks the box from above.
no change to the appliances at all
per pass: fridge 2.7 kJ, freezer 8.8 kJ + 1 g ice
FRONT VIEW, drawer fronts facing the shaft
ZOOM: the shaft between a fridge and a freezer unit
B: 2 shells with top exits = 1,200 mm
an open drawer spills its cold air: 90–125 L
per pass, about 10× the top hatch
freezer: about 1 g of rime on the boxes per pass
six small appliances use more energy than two
K9b allots 1,200 mm for cold storage
Good: zero appliance change, easy for people,
and a dual-zone unit gives the 10 °C cool zone.

g.text: 1/6 Drawer fridges and freezers are used unmodified, turned 90° so that their drawers open into a shaft between them.
2/6 A lift in the shaft hooks the drawer's pull bar and pulls the drawer 450 mm out into the shaft.
3/6 The gallery hoist lowers on a long rope (up to 1.7 m) and picks the box from above: boxes stand in one layer, no digging.
4/6 The drawer goes back in: it was open about 9 s for one box, at the edge of the 10 s limit.
5/6 Freezer drawer: the open drawer spills its cold air (90–125 L per pass), and humid air leaves rime on every box in it.
6/6 No change to the appliances and easy access for people, but six units need about 2.7 m of wall and €9,000–17,000.
